statements.t: This summary is not intended to be exhaustive, nor is it intended to be a substitute for the detailed discussion and analysis provided elsewhere in this Quarterly Report, including our condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes.

We anticipate growing demand for our Apollo TM platform, led in the near-term by Non-Automotive markets such as aerospace and defense, intelligent transportation systems, or ITS, railway, airport safety and security, perimeter monitoring, space mobility, transportation logistics, and sports analytics.

However, as our customers continue their R&D projects to commercialize solutions that rely on lidar technology, it is difficult to estimate the timing of ultimate end market demand and customer adoption.

While the automotive market for lidar is projected to grow over the mid- and long-term, we expect automotive programs to represent a smaller portion of our revenue than non-automotive markets for the foreseeable future, and our near-term financial performance to be driven primarily by non-automotive customers.
We anticipate that Non‑Automotive applications will be a more significant driver of our near‑term revenue given the generally shorter sales cycles and development timelines in these markets.

We have unified our supply chain for the Automotive and Non-Automotive markets and leverage our Tier 1 automotive suppliers to produce products for us to sell into our Non-Automotive markets, whereas in the Automotive markets, any participation would be expected to occur through our Tier 1 partners, which may include licensing arrangements.
By leveraging ATI's and LighTekton's extensive networks and manufacturing capabilities, we aim to accelerate our market penetration and deliver our advanced lidar solutions to a broader audience.

There can be no assurance that either selection will result in additional orders or commercial sales for us, or that we will be able to successfully address the technical and operational requirements of these new markets.
We are being evaluated for expanded use cases with these customers, and expect to receive additional requests for quotation in the near term.

Delays in autonomy programs by OEMs that we are currently or plan to be working with through our Tier 1 partners could result in us being unable to achieve our revenue and profitability targets in the time frame we anticipate, or at all.

As production volumes increase, we expect product costs to continue to decline through bill-of-material reductions and manufacturing efficiencies; however, there can be no assurance that we will achieve these reductions or positive gross margins

Unlike traditional sensing systems that passively collect data, our active Intelligent Sensing Platform employs principles from automated targeting systems and biomimicry to actively scan the environment, intelligently focusing on critical elements to enable safer, smarter, and faster decisions in complex scenarios.
Several partners are also exploring new platforms based on our Apollo TM architecture and have initiated discussions on development work, which we expect will increase over time.
As we increase the volume of Apollo TM units that are manufactured, we expect the bill of materials costs to decrease over time.

We expect our R&D costs to increase as we continue to invest in product development, expanded product variations, and commercialization efforts; however, we anticipate these increases will occur at a more moderate pace relative to our investment in sales and marketing as we prioritize execution and near‑term commercial opportunities.

We expect our S&M expenses to increase as we pursue Non-Automotive opportunities to accelerate profitability while continuing to leverage our Tier 1 partners to commercialize our products and manage relationships with the OEMs in the Automotive market.

We expect our G&A expenses, excluding stock-based compensation, to be more moderate going forward as we leverage the public company infrastructure we have built; however, stock-based compensation, including expense related to market-based awards, may cause G&A expenses to fluctuate from period to period.

We expect the change in fair value of warrant liabilities to decrease as the warrant associated with the 2022 Note was cancelled, the warrant associated with the 2025 Note was exercised in full in 2025, and the Private Placement Warrants expired in August 2026.
We expect that our expenses will continue to exceed our operating income and, as a result, we may need additional capital resources to fund our operations.

estimates.t: Our condensed consolidated financial statements are in accordance with GAAP.

statements.t: We expect to continue converting our record pipeline into sustained commercial activity, leading to significant revenue growth anticipated in 2027.

Our visibility into this expected revenue ramp includes a combination of repeat product purchases, commercial programs, and new opportunities, supported by a go-to-market strategy designed to serve a growing number of high-growth markets.”

“With Lunar Outpost ramping alongside repeat sensor orders, we expect the fourth quarter to be our first million dollar revenue quarter driven mainly by Apollo™ commercial programs, establishing a new expected quarterly baseline as we build toward 2027.”

We are targeting an approximately 15% reduction in cash consumption in 2027, and with $63.1 million in cash and marketable securities and a virtually debt free balance sheet, we believe we have the capacity to support our customers’ programs through the ramp.”

For the fourth quarter 2026, revenue is expected to approximately double third quarter 2026 revenue and be the Company’s first $1 million revenue quarter, driven mainly by Apollo™ commercial programs.
The Company expects that cash consumption for the full year 2026 will be $35 million, inclusive of approximately $5 million in working capital to support the commercial ramp.
The Company is aiming to lower 2027 cash consumption by approximately 15% from the 2026 expected cash consumption level.
